subject: Proposal: short-term p95 padding and regional fallback for EU hosted API
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starchart.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@starchart.ai
Date: 2027-07-28T09:15:00Z
Subject: Hosted API p95 behavior in eu-west-1 - request for short-term allowance

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from our ops team: over the last two weeks we've seen intermittent p95 spikes for the EU region around high-traffic batch jobs (~03:00-04:30 UTC). Baseline p50 looks fine, but p95 is exceeding our contract target by ~120-180ms for short periods (15-45m). We've attached a CSV with captures (slo-capture-20270720.csv).

We're not asking for a permanent SLA change, but would like to request a temporary accommodation while we rework our batching to smooth load. Two asks: 1) a short-term p95 padding (suggest +150ms) for eu-west-1 for up to 90 days; and 2) an agreed regional fallback to a compatible, slightly smaller model if latency breaches the amended p95 during peak windows.

Can you share what you need from our side to evaluate? Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Ops, Starchart AI

Attachment: slo-capture-20270720.csv (CSV, 147KB)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starchart.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-30T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 behavior in eu-west-1 - request for short-term allowance

Hi Marta — thanks for the data and clear asks. I reviewed the CSV and flagged it to engineering; summary below and a short proposal for a trial amendment.

Summary of what we see:
- p50 across your traffic remains comfortably within the committed target.
- p95 shows short-lived spikes correlated with your nightly batch windows (approx 03:00-04:30 UTC).
- Root cause appears to be bursty concurrency leading to transient queueing on the shard serving eu-west-1.

Suggested approach (temporary, controlled):
1) Short-term p95 padding: Redwood proposes a 90-day amendment that applies only to eu-west-1 production traffic for Starchart AI. During the amendment, the effective contractual p95 will be the committed p95 + 125ms.
2) Regional fallback policy: implement an automated fallback to a verified smaller model variant (quantized) when observed P95 breaches the amended threshold for >5 consecutive minutes. This preserves availability while bounding quality regression.
3) Measurement window & evidence: We'll measure p50/p95 on a 60s rolling window (server-side aggregation) and provide daily evidence reports during the trial.

Next steps we need from Starchart:
- Confirmation you agree to the 90-day trial and rollback conditions.
- Approval to run the fallback in your eu-west-1 fleet (we will only use model variants you have already approved).
- A brief technical contact for the kickoff.

I've attached a short brief (proposed-amendment-brief.pdf) and included Ben (sales) and Karthik (serving/runtime) on the thread. If this looks good I can draft the contract addendum and Rishi will propose credits.

Proposed kickoff: 2027-08-04 if that works for you.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-amendment-brief.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@starchart.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Re: Hosted API p95 behavior in eu-west-1 - request for short-term allowance

Lauren / Marta — quick technical gloss and operational constraints from the runtime side.

Notes:
- Measurement window: 60s rolling window is OK for evidence reports, but our internal SLO engine aggregates percentile over 5m epochs for SLA triggers. For the amendment we can expose both: 60s for daily evidence and 5m epochs for automated fallback gating.
- Fallback tuning: the smaller model variant must be pre-warmed in eu-west-1 (persistent cache warm) before we enable auto-fallback; otherwise fallback could itself add latency while cold-starting. We recommend a warm cache threshold + a 2-minute cooldown before reverting to primary.
- KV cache considerations: your workload shows heavy per-user KV reuse during the batch windows — small changes to client-side prefixing would reduce jitter. We'll help with a short checklist.

Operational plan (high-level):
1) Pre-warm fallback variant (we'll coordinate a small allocation for warm cache).
2) Enable amendment with conservative threshold: amended p95 = contractual_p95 + 125ms. Automated fallback will trigger if 5m epoch p95 > amended threshold AND 60s rolling is > amended threshold for 2 consecutive samples.
3) Daily evidence reports and weekly sync for the first month.

If you want, I can paste the exact config snippet for our routing policy in the kickoff.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
